title: [Chapitre] VII. Analysis situs (troisième mouture) : notes manuscrites (23-26/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: in the 1986 'Analysis situs' notes Grothendieck axiomatizes 'ateliers'. These are combinatorial models of a tame-topological or polyhedral space. M is a set of 'lieux' (figures), ordered by inclusion ≤, with a second relation ≪ (and an underlined/strict variant, written ⋐ here). L ⊂ M is the set of minimal elements ('points'). A further relation ∥ is used, called 'ligature' on p.39, which here behaves like a separation or distinguishability relation. On p.37 he shows how (M, ≤, ≪), with ∥ given on M, can be recovered from axioms ML. He adds the polyhedral variant ML0 pol: each M_{≤X} is a polyhedral poset, meaning bounded pairs have infima.

Page 38 reverses the question. Starting from (M, ≤, ≪) alone, how much freedom is there in choosing ∥ on the points? A choice of ∥ amounts to a subset Γ of P_2(L), the unordered pairs of points (a symmetric relation). He defines a minimal set Γ_0. A pair {x,y} lies in Γ_0 iff there are figures Y ≤ X with y ⋐ Y and x ⋐ X but x not ≤ Y. In words: y lies in a subfigure Y of X that does not contain x, so the configuration itself forces x and y to be told apart. The claim is that any Γ with Γ_0 ⊂ Γ ⊂ P_2(L) is an admissible parallelism or ligature structure. He remarks 'Ça fait de la marge!' and notes that later one must see how the axioms (the At-type axioms of ateliers) cut down this freedom. He lists the cases he currently has in mind:
- some At-variant (cf. p.18);
- 'At eucl' and its variants (cf. 'GF VI, p.52', an internal reference).

A marginal note then asks: for a set-theoretic (resp. polyhedral) realization, must one demand x ∥ y ⇒ x ≠ y (irreflexivity)? He answers 'probably not'. His reason is that this imposes no restriction on ≤ and ≪. Moreover, the conditions ML0–ML3 imply neither that the natural map M → Fig(L) (figure ↦ its set of points) is injective, nor that ⋐ is induced by the corresponding relation ≪ between set-theoretic figures in L. So the abstract structure is genuinely more general than point-set realizations. The next page restarts the theory with a 'dense' subset Λ ⊂ M replacing L.
errors: Possible slip in the definition of Γ_0: the condition 'y ⋐ X' is crossed out in the manuscript and presumably replaced by 'y ⋐ Y'. Only with Y does the definition make sense: x lies in X but not in the subfigure Y that contains y.

The claim that every Γ ⊇ Γ_0 works is asserted without proof on this page. It presumably refers to the ML axioms of p.37, and its validity depends on which At axioms are imposed. He himself notes that the axioms will restrict the choice later.

If P_2(L) means 2-element subsets, then x≠y is automatic. The marginal question about x∥y ⇒ x≠y suggests P_2 includes singletons (subsets of cardinality ≤2), or else the question is about non-injective realizations. This is slightly ambiguous.

ideas.what: Axiomatic 'ateliers': combinatorial structures (M, ≤, ≪, ∥) of figures with points L as minimal elements, meant to model tame or polyhedral spaces.
ideas.modern_name: combinatorial / o-minimal-style tame topology; posets of strata; closest notions are face posets and cell-complex posets
ideas.usually_credited_to: o-minimality (van den Dries, Pillay–Steinhorn, Knight) for tame topology. Grothendieck's ateliers themselves are unpublished.
ideas.where_published: Tame topology is called for in Esquisse d'un programme (1984), but the atelier formalism is only in the Montpellier archive notes.

ideas.what: Lower bound Γ_0 on a separation/ligature relation: pairs of points forced to be distinguished by a nested pair of figures. Any symmetric Γ ⊇ Γ_0 is admissible.
ideas.modern_name: a symmetric relation containing a minimal 'separation' relation; reminiscent of apartness relations / T0-type distinguishability
ideas.usually_credited_to: Apartness: Brouwer/Heyting. Specialization/T0 distinguishability: standard topology.

ideas.what: Observation that abstract atelier data need not be set-theoretically realized: M → Fig(L) need not be injective, and ≪ on M need not be induced from point sets.
ideas.modern_name: non-spatial (pointless) structures vs. spatial ones; sober/spatial locales analogy

missed.claim: Grothendieck leaves open how the atelier axioms (At, At eucl and variants) restrict the admissible ligature relations Γ between Γ_0 and P_2(L). This is a classification question that was never carried out, since the atelier framework was never published.
missed.quote: Ça fait de la marge! Pour la suite, il faudra voir comment les axiomes restreignent le choix
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Only of interest to someone reconstructing Grothendieck's axiomatic tame topology. Taken in isolation it is a modest combinatorial question.

missed.claim: His relation ∥ on points, with a forced minimal part Γ_0 and the explicit decision not to impose irreflexivity, behaves like a generalized apartness/separation relation. It also resembles the distinction between spatial and non-spatial (pointless) structures. Grothendieck does not make this link explicitly.
missed.quote: faut-il pas x ∥ y ⇒ x ≠ y ?? Sans doute pas
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Slight. It could help situate the atelier formalism relative to locale theory and constructive topology.

deep.surprise_reason: This is an internal step in an unpublished axiomatic framework (ateliers). The content of the page, a lower bound Γ_0 and the remark that the realization map need not be injective, is elementary. Interest lies only in documenting the unpublished 'analysis situs' program.
transcription_corrections: In Γ_0 the crossed-out 'X' after 'y ⋐' is presumably replaced by 'Y', as the transcription already suggests.
'la marge semble [?] :' → more likely 'Pour le moment, j'en vois surtout :' (reading of the line after '∥ (et des autres)').
'At [?] ... (cf p. [?] 18)' → line reads roughly 'At s...vr (cf p. 18)'; the name is illegible.
'Pour quoi a-t-on une relation spéciale ensembliste' → likely 'Pour qu'on ait une réalisation ensembliste (resp. polyédrale), faut-il pas x ∥ y ⇒ x ≠ y ??'.
'M C0 : M L 3' → 'ML0 à ML3' (axioms ML0–ML3).
